t.5.61.1: Then the bull among monkeys, his heart troubled at the mere sight of the monkey who had fallen at his feet with his head bowed to the ground, spoke these words.
t.5.61.2: Rise, rise! Why have you fallen at my feet? Let there be no fear for you, O hero; let only the truth be spoken.
t.5.61.3: But he, the greatly wise Dadhimukha, having been reassured by that great-souled Sugrīva, rose up and spoke these words.
t.5.61.4: O king, this grove was never before granted for their use, neither by Ṛkṣarajas, nor by you, nor even by Vālin; yet it has been devoured by the monkeys.
t.5.61.5: The forest guards have been assailed by these monkeys, and though restrained by those guards, they pay them no heed and go on eating and drinking the honey.
t.5.61.6: Some here fling away what is left, while others eat it; and when they are restrained, all of them simply knit their eyebrows in a frown.
t.5.61.7: For these, though greatly enraged, were overpowered in this way by those furious bulls among the monkeys as they tried to keep them out of that grove.
t.5.61.8: Then those many heroic monkeys, their eyes reddened with anger, drove back the monkeys, those bulls among monkeys.
t.5.61.9: Some were struck down with their hands, others battered with their knees; they were dragged about at will and shown the path of the gods.
t.5.61.11: Then Lakṣmaṇa, the greatly wise slayer of enemy heroes, questioned Sugrīva, the bull among monkeys, as he was being informed in this way.
t.5.61.10: Thus have these heroes been struck down, even while you, their master, stand by, and the whole of Madhuvana is being devoured by them at their pleasure.
t.5.61.12: O king, why has this monkey, the guardian of the forest, come here? And with what matter in view did he speak these words in such distress?
t.5.61.13: Thus addressed by the great-souled Lakṣmaṇa, Sugrīva, skilled in speech, spoke these words in reply to Lakṣmaṇa.
t.5.61.14: O noble Lakṣmaṇa, the valiant monkey Dadhimukha has reported that the honey has been eaten by the heroic monkeys led by Aṅgada.
t.5.61.15: Such boldness would not be theirs had they not fulfilled their task; from the way the grove has been overrun by them, the work has surely been accomplished by the monkeys.
t.5.61.17: In Hanumān, that bull among monkeys, are firmly established the accomplishment of the task, wisdom, resolve, valour, and learning as well.
t.5.61.16: The queen has been seen, there is no doubt, and by none other than Hanumān. For no one other than Hanumān could be the means of accomplishing this deed.
t.5.61.18: Where Jāmbavān, lord of the forces, is Aṅgada's guide, and Hanumān too is the overseer, the outcome of that venture cannot be otherwise.
t.5.61.20: How the Madhuvana was entered by those monkeys when they arrived, and how the entire grove was ravaged and its honey consumed by them; and how the guards, though standing together, were held back and struck with their knees.
t.5.61.19: The Madhuvana, it is said, has been laid waste by the heroes led by Aṅgada, those bulls among monkeys who have come back after searching the southern quarter.
t.5.61.21: For this very purpose has he come here to speak, this sweet-spoken monkey named Dadhimukha, renowned for his valour.
t.5.61.22: Sītā has been seen, O mighty-armed Saumitri; see the truth of it, for all the monkeys have come there and are drinking the honey.
t.5.61.24: Then, having heard the words pleasing to the ear that fell from Sugrīva's mouth, the righteous-souled Lakṣmaṇa, together with Rāghava, was filled with delight.
t.5.61.25: Hearing these words of Dadhimukha, Rāma rejoiced greatly, and so did the greatly renowned Lakṣmaṇa; and Sugrīva, delighted, spoke again in reply to the guardian of the grove.
t.5.61.23: O bull among men, these renowned forest-dwellers would never have ravaged the divine grove, granted as a boon, had they not seen Vaidehī.
t.5.61.26: I am pleased, gentle one, that the grove has been enjoyed by those who have accomplished their task; the conduct of those who have accomplished their task is forgiven, and indeed deserves to be forgiven.
t.5.61.27: Together with the two Rāghavas, I wish to see at once those monkeys led by Hanumān, proud as the king of beasts, who have accomplished their purpose, and to hear of their efforts in finding Sītā.
